entries.title: Job 41:1
segments:
Levithan; supposed by some to be the whale, by others, the crocodile, with which latter animal the description best agrees. 
 
The principal superiority of man above many of the beasts consists not in his sizer or strength of body, but in the faculties and powers of his mind; and the cultivation and right use of these should be his chief concern.

entries.title: Job 41:6
segments: The companions; the companies of fishermen.

entries.title: Job 41:7
segments: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons?--with fish-spears? the bony armor or scales of the crocodile's skin make it impenetrable to spears, or even musket-balls, except in particular parts.

entries.title: Job 41:8
segments: Remember the battle; think of the conflict that would ensue should you attempt to take him, and refrain from it.

entries.title: Job 41:9
segments: The hope of him; the hope of taking him; or, the hope of him who would take him.

entries.title: Job 41:11
segments:
Prevented me; gone before me in the bestowment of favors, and laid me under obligation to repay them. 
 
None can devote any thing to God which He has not first given to them, or lay him under obligations to bestow any good upon them; but all must depend on his goodness, mercy, and grace.

entries.title: Job 41:13
segments:
Discover the face of his garment? strip off his skin. 
 
  Come to him with his double bridle? or, Come within his double bridle, a figurative expresson for his two rows of teeth.

entries.title: Job 41:14
segments: The doors of his face? his jaws.

entries.title: Job 41:18
segments:
Neesings; sneezing, or violent breathing, as when he comes to the surface after being some time under the water. 
 
  A light doth shine; the reference here, and in the following verses, seems to be to the white spray glittering in the sun, which he throws with violence from his mouth and nostrils.

entries.title: Job 41:22
segments: Sorrow is turned into joy; this some have translated, terror danceth before him.

entries.title: Job 41:25
segments:
By reason of breakings they purify themselves; or, they lose themselves with terror. 
 
The fear of man which is impressed upon most of the animal tribes, and which adds so much to his safety and comfort, is a striking evidence of the goodness of God; and lays men under obligations to employ the influence he has given for the good of all.

entries.title: Job 41:30
segments: Sharp stones; rather, sharp pieces of potsherd.  These, and the "sharp pointed things," refer to the sharp protuberances on his belly.

entries.title: Job 41:32
segments: He maketh a path to shine after him; makes the deep white with foam.

entries.title: Job 41:34
segments: The children of pride; the most strong and courageous of the animal creation.
